question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{XY}{3}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2x,\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3-3x; \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=\frac{xy}{3}.
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3-3x\},$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14270831/assets/b5a9355f0c2a39a1da71f3132c1eb3d7c72464af62b23f8a26d76df306bf9773.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{XY}{3}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}\frac{xy}{3}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{xy}{3}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x}\frac{xy}{3}\cdot 2x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=3-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(3-3x)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}({x}^{2}-2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =3[\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
